title: Reddit is putting more limits on Old.Reddit.com
gist: Reddit will limit Old.Reddit.com to logged-in users who have used Old Reddit in the past six months (moderators excepted) and will end RSS support on November 13, citing scraping and automated abuse. Reddit says it is not shutting Old Reddit down, but the author argues that shrinking usage will make closure easier to justify later.

insights.claim: In the next few months Reddit will restrict Old.Reddit.com to logged-in users who have used Old Reddit within the last six months, with an exception for logged-in moderators.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Reddit is closing low-friction data access paths, which protects the value of its data-licensing business.

insights.claim: Reddit will stop supporting RSS feeds on November 13 because RSS has become a common surface for large-scale scraping. Moderators get supported alternatives such as Devvit apps, but there is no replacement for other RSS users.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Another open-web data channel is being closed as platforms protect content that AI companies want.

insights.claim: In 2025 CEO Steve Huffman said Old Reddit would stay online as long as people used it, but in August he said changes were needed, probably including limited access, migrating important uses and rebuilding it on a modern tech stack.
insights.speaker: Scharon Harding
insights.so_what: Management's position on legacy products has clearly changed.
insights.quote: the reality is we’re getting to that time where we need to make some changes.
